prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1022; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left lane on a Sugar Land roadway when Driver 2, operating a vehicle in the adjacent lane, began a lane change without confirming the lane was clear. The two vehicles made contact along their right and left sides, respectively, with the force of the contact consistent with the damage observed on both vehicles. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred as Driver 1 described it, and Driver 1's account was consistent with the physical evidence at the scene. Photographs taken by the responding officer show damage that is largely in line with a sideswipe of this type. Two independent witnesses, who were stopped at a nearby traffic signal, gave statements confirming the sequence of events. A Passenger was also present in Driver 1's vehicle and was identified at the scene. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder, which is consistent with the mechanism of the collision as described by all parties. No prior damage to the vehicle was known to the involved parties or observed by the responding officer. Driver 1 was identified as a household member of the registered policyholder, who was not present at the scene.
